newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real drops 0.05 pct in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real drops 0.05 pct in quiet trading.

text.p: Brazil's real dropped 0.05 percent on Tuesday to close at 1.0815 per dollar in quiet trading in the commercial foreign exchange market, dealers said.

Dealers said the real's decline partially reflected dollar outflows. At 1645 local/1945 GMT, preliminary figures for commercial and financial forex contracts in the commercial foreign exchange market showed a $35 million deficit.
But dealers said they would not be surprised if the forex contracts show a slight net dollar inflow by the end of the day.

They also said expectations of a decline in the reais-dollar mini-band in coming days put pressure on the Brazilian currency. The current mini-band was set by the Central Bank on Thursday at between 1.0810 and 1.0860 reais per dollar.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real closed flat at 1.0865 per dollar.
In the parallel market, the real dropped 0.44 percent to end at 1.147 per dollar, traders said.
